# contentful_entry (Resource)

Manages a Contentful Entry in an environment. Creating an Entry or changing its managed fields or metadata writes and publishes a draft. Import and refresh do not publish drafts written outside Terraform.

## Example Usage

Use the [Author Content Type example](content_type#example-usage) in the same configuration. This Entry sets the author's name in `en-US`. Use the environment's default locale code if it differs.

```terraform
resource "contentful_entry" "example" {
  space_id        = contentful_content_type.author.space_id
  environment_id  = contentful_content_type.author.environment_id
  content_type_id = contentful_content_type.author.content_type_id

  fields = {
    name = { "en-US" = jsonencode("Ursula Le Guin") }
  }
}
```

Routine provider logs omit Entry request and response payloads. Contentful error diagnostics can still contain Entry content, even when its Terraform expression is sensitive. Review diagnostics before sharing them. See [Secrets and Terraform state](../guides/secrets-and-state) for storage and redaction behavior.

## Drift and field ownership

- Outside pending draft recovery, changing only `timeouts` leaves the remote Entry untouched.
- Unpublishing outside Terraform makes `published_version` null. Terraform does not republish solely to restore the previous publication. A later managed `fields` or `metadata` change writes and publishes a new draft.
- To leave one translation to another editor, add its path to `lifecycle.ignore_changes`, for example `fields["name"]["fr-FR"]`. Entry updates replace the complete `fields` payload. Values retained by `ignore_changes` remain in that payload and are published with any later managed change. An ignored-only external draft is left untouched.
- Content Type defaults may be added when an Entry is created, but Contentful does not reapply them on updates. Use `ignore_changes` for defaulted fields that another system should continue to manage.
- The resource uses whole-Entry publication and does not model independent locale publication. Locale-based publishing is currently unsupported.

## Null and empty field values

A Terraform `null` map element omits that field or locale from the request. To send JSON null for a translation, use `name = { "en-US" = jsonencode(null) }`. Refresh preserves a previously omitted null element while it is absent. A returned value takes precedence so external changes remain visible.

Contentful can omit fields whose locale values are all empty arrays. The provider preserves those known empty values while absent. A removed nonempty value remains observable.

## Upgrading Entry fields

Earlier configurations encoded each complete locale map as one JSON string. Move `jsonencode` to each locale value. For example, change `name = jsonencode({ "en-US" = var.name })` to `name = { "en-US" = jsonencode(var.name) }`. Expressions producing maps of JSON strings and module inputs with type `map(string)` need the same change at their source. From the provider source checkout, run `go run ./cmd/terraform-provider-contentful-migrate -check /path/to/config` to identify safe literal conversions and skipped expressions. Use `-write` to rewrite supported literals, review the diff, and convert dynamic expressions and module variable types manually. A subsequent `-check` exits nonzero while changes or skipped expressions remain. The provider upgrades supported prior state at plan time. Review the plan before applying.

The earlier whole-field expression `name = jsonencode(null)` sent a JSON null in place of the entire locale map. The nested schema cannot express that value. State upgrade reports the field path and stops if it encounters whole-field JSON null. Keep the previous provider version while that behavior is required.

## Destroy

Destroy unpublishes the Entry, then deletes it. If unpublishing fails for a reason other than an already absent or unpublished Entry, deletion stops. Contentful does not enforce version or ETag preconditions on these requests, so changes made outside Terraform since the last refresh do not prevent deletion.

## Publication recovery

If publication fails after Contentful accepts a draft, inspect the Entry and run `terraform plan`. Creation can finish with a warning. A `VersionMismatch` ends automatic recovery immediately, including on the first publication attempt. An unchanged apply then leaves the draft alone.

For other publication request failures, Terraform can retry the recorded draft version without writing it again. Refresh checks that the same draft still needs publication. If the original draft write was never confirmed, Terraform has no version it can safely publish. See [recovery after a failed write](../guides/operation-timeouts#recover-after-a-failed-write).

If creation failed before Terraform saved a generated `entry_id`, look for the Entry in Contentful. [Import](#import) it before retrying to avoid creating a duplicate.

## Schema

### Required

- `content_type_id` (String) ID of the content type for this entry. Changing this value replaces the resource.
- `environment_id` (String) ID of the environment containing the entry. Changing this value replaces the resource.
- `fields` (Map of Map of String) Complete set of Entry field values, keyed by Contentful field ID and locale code. Encode each locale value with jsonencode. Use the environment's default locale for non-localized fields. Updates replace the complete fields payload. See [field ownership](#drift-and-field-ownership) and [null and empty values](#null-and-empty-field-values).
- `space_id` (String) ID of the space containing the entry. Changing this value replaces the resource.

### Optional

- `entry_id` (String) ID of the entry. Omit to let Contentful generate an ID. When configured, Terraform creates a new Entry with that ID; an existing Entry with the same ID must be imported before management. Changing this value replaces the resource.
- `metadata` (Attributes) Tags and taxonomy concepts assigned to the entry. Defaults to empty lists for both tags and concepts. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--metadata))
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Composite Terraform resource identifier in `space_id/environment_id/entry_id` form.
- `published_version` (Number) Contentful `sys.publishedVersion` for the Entry. Null when Contentful reports the Entry as unpublished.

<a id="nestedatt--metadata"></a>
### Nested Schema for `metadata`

Optional:

- `concepts` (List of String) IDs of Contentful taxonomy concepts attached to the Entry. Configured IDs must be unique. Reordering alone may update Terraform state but does not write or publish the Entry.
- `tags` (List of String) IDs of Contentful tags attached to the Entry. Configured IDs must be unique. Reordering alone may update Terraform state but does not write or publish the Entry.


<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) Duration for the complete operation, including retries, for example `30s` or `5m`. Defaults to `2m`.
- `delete` (String) Includes retries and uses the duration saved in state (default `2m`, minimum provider timeout `10s`).
- `read` (String) Includes retries and uses the duration saved in state (default `2m`, minimum provider timeout `10s`).
- `update` (String) Duration for the complete operation, including retries, for example `30s` or `5m`. Defaults to `2m`.

## Import

### By identity (Terraform 1.12 or later)

```terraform
import {
  identity = {
    space_id       = var.contentful_space_id
    environment_id = var.contentful_environment_id
    entry_id       = var.entry_id
  }
  to = contentful_entry.example
}
```

### By ID (Terraform 1.5 or later)

```terraform
import {
  id = "${var.contentful_space_id}/${var.contentful_environment_id}/${var.entry_id}"
  to = contentful_entry.example
}
```

### From the command line

```shell
terraform import contentful_entry.example "$CONTENTFUL_SPACE_ID/$CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID/$CONTENTFUL_ENTRY_ID"
```
